product: GroundingWell (550+ ads live; overheard-question angle: hotel guests asking what mattress they use)
hook: If you're in ecom / Pay the f*ck attention to what GroundingWell is doing with their creative right now
body: GroundingWell runs 550+ ads; the winning angle is hotel guests asking what mattress they use -- and they don't even sell mattresses. The transcript is the overheard-question scene: a wedding guest asks Sarah what mattress the hotel uses; she saved three grand; half the calls are about the sheets; ordering one tonight.
idea: The overheard question: a stranger's genuine-sounding question about the product (what mattress is this?) becomes the ad -- they don't even sell the hero object.
sequencing: The angle: hotel guests asking about the mattress
The twist: they don't sell mattresses
The payoff: saved three grand, ordering tonight
formatting: X post with photo and a 108s video (video.twimg.com, 720x1280) plus transcript.
why_it_works: The question is the hook: overhearing a stranger ask about something triggers the same curiosity as gossip; the twist (not their product) keeps it from feeling like an ad.
what_to_steal: The overheard-question angle for Louise Carter: strangers stopping to ask where are those earrings from / is that real gold -- the jewelry is the answer to someone else's question.

idea: Free-product street interviews for genuine reactions: proven organic, unproven for paid -- an open test.
sequencing: The mechanics (free product, fun questions, genuine reactions)
why_it_works: Asking the community turns the post into a research thread.
what_to_steal: Test the free-product street interview for Louise Carter: hand pieces to strangers, ask fun questions, capture genuine reactions -- and answer the paid question with a real test.

product: unnamed cortisol/weight supplement (AI resort random-interview ad; Are you really 56?)
hook: This might be the most convincing AI ad format I've seen yet. / It looks like a random interview at a resort. / Are you really 56?
body: The AI resort interview: an overheard-style opener (I overheard you talking with friend), the age hook (Are you really 56?), the drops (lost 18 pounds in one month, love handles were never from food, it was cortisol), the mechanism (stress hormones, dieting failed), and the product (two pills a day, try it today). Story first, product second.
idea: The resort random interview: an overheard question plus an unbelievable-but-specific claim (56, 18 pounds, cortisol) makes AI feel unscripted and native.
formatting: X post with a 45s video (video.twimg.com, 720x1280) and full transcript.
why_it_works: Specific numbers (56, 18 pounds, one month) make the unbelievable believable; the overheard framing dodges the interview's staged feel.
what_to_steal: The overheard-opener + specific-number combo for Louise Carter: I overheard you... + a specific jewelry claim (3 years, still no tarnish) in a resort/beach interview.

hook: Ranking every type of ecom ad creative format:

Street interviews sit in F tier here.

what_to_steal: The warning: generic street interviews are F tier -- Louise Carter's must be overheard-question grade (specific, surprising) to escape the tier.

hook: This ad format just won't die... / The man on the street interview.
body: The practitioner's note: the man-on-the-street interview isn't new but keeps working across clients. Why: it's natural -- viewers are hooked to see why she is being stopped on the street.
idea: The format's durability: viewers stay to learn why someone was stopped -- the stop itself is the hook.
sequencing: The why: why is she being stopped?
why_it_works: The stop creates an open loop that only the interview resolves.
what_to_steal: Build every Louise Carter street interview around the stop: the opening 2 seconds must make viewers ask why she was stopped (the jewelry is the answer).

product: unnamed pet brand ($29K -> $150K/mo spend in 60 days; CPA $188 -> $124)
hook: Just run ads that don't look like ads
body: The stealth-ads thesis: UGC is predictable (Andromeda reads 50 near-identical UGC videos as one ad), over-polished ads die in frame one, discount statics train sale-waiting, influencer whitelisting is un-iterable. Stealth ads (podcast clips, street interviews, skits) look like content: the first 3 seconds feel organic, one angle runs in 5 formats (Meta reads each as new), volume without new casting, the format carries authority so the product comes late, fatigue slows, studio actors mean owned footage. Proof: pet brand $29K -> $150K/mo in 60 days, CPA $188 -> $124, ~95% of creatives changed, same campaign structure.
idea: Stealth beats polish: podcast clips, street interviews, and skits look like content, so hooks get a real chance -- and one angle in 5 formats reads as 5 new ads to Meta.
sequencing: The closer: just run ads that don't look like ads
formatting: Long-form X essay post; no media in the excerpt.
why_it_works: The four-format autopsy makes stealth feel like the only rational choice; the pet-brand numbers prove it.
what_to_steal: The stealth portfolio for Louise Carter: street interviews and podcast clips as the always-on formats, one winning angle rendered in 5 formats, product entering late.
